title: Tenali Raman and the Rope Made of Ashes

keywords: the challenge of making a rope from ashes
full_text:
An ambassador from a rival northern sultanate arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, presenting an extraordinary challenge from his sovereign:
'O Emperor Krishnadevaraya! My Sultan desires to test whether your famed courtiers possess true philosophical magic.
You must deliver to our capital within seven days a rope twenty cubits long woven entirely of pure ash!
If your court fails, Vijayanagara must pay a tribute of five thousand gold coins!'

The King and his ministers were in despair. Ash is powdery, crumbly, and has no fiber; as soon as one touches it, it dissolves into dust.
'How can anyone weave a rope out of ash?' groaned the Prime Minister.

Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, weaving a rope of ash is simple. Permit me to prepare it tonight.'

Tenali took a sturdy, well-twisted hemp rope measuring precisely twenty cubits in length.
He laid the rope flat in a straight, neat line upon a wide, flat granite slab in the palace courtyard.
He soaked the rope lightly in sesame oil and camphor, and then set fire to one end.
The flame burned steadily down the length of the rope without disturbing its woven twists.
When the fire burned out and the smoke cleared, the charred remains lay upon the granite slab completely undisturbed:
Every twist, braid, and fiber was preserved perfectly—yet the entire rope was made of solid, pure white and grey ash!

The next morning, Tenali invited the foreign ambassador and King Krishnadevaraya to the courtyard.
Pointing to the granite slab, Tenali said:
'Behold, noble ambassador! Here is your rope of pure ash, precisely twenty cubits long, woven with flawless braids!
Now, I pray thee: pick it up gently with your own hands and carry it to your Sultan!'

The ambassador reached down eagerly to pick it up—but the moment his fingers touched the fragile ash, the braid crumbled into powder between his fingers!

The ambassador gasped in embarrassment: 'I cannot lift it! It falls apart!'

Tenali smiled with dazzling triumph:
'Ah, noble envoy! My Emperor commanded me to make the rope of ash, and I have made it.
If your Sultan wishes to possess it, he must provide servants who know how to lift a rope of ash without breaking it!
Bring your carrying cases of cloud and wind to pack it, or acknowledge the superiority of Vijayanagara!'

The ambassador blushed, bowed low, and withdrew his challenge with profound apologies.
King Krishnadevaraya rewarded Tenali with a diamond armlet, celebrating that wit can answer any impossible puzzle.
moral: Impossible demands are best answered by demanding the impossible conditions necessary to receive them.
